{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZXRbmw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC-kkg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 29, "title": "Resolve reverse $2180-to-WRAM DMA/HDMA conflicts and implement supported side effects", "body": "## Problem

Reverse WMDATA-to-WRAM transfers currently execute ordinary memory copies. `SystemBus::transfer` reads `$2180`, advancing its 17-bit pointer, then writes the returned byte to the A-bus destination. Forward conflict suppression does not cover this direction. See [transfer handling](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f3e56850b0a9f6584a3086749e6a1647ae93a70/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L431) and [WMDATA reads](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f3e56850b0a9f6584a3086749e6a1647ae93a70/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L268).

The latest assessment identifies this as the next incomplete hardware behavior. Issues #25 and #27 implemented forward restrictions; neither established reverse memory-write or pointer side effects. Existing tests deliberately avoid conflicting reverse transfers and cover legal WMDATA-to-SRAM transfers instead. See [current reverse coverage](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f3e56850b0a9f6584a3086749e6a1647ae93a70/crates/snes-core/src/machine/dma_tests.rs#L811).

A specification prerequisite is necessary: the repository's recorded quotations establish forward suppression, but do not establish whether reverse conflicts suppress the A-bus write, prevent pointer advancement, or write an unspecified byte. Extending the forward rule unchanged would create an unsupported contract.

## Expected outcome

Establish a direction-specific contract for reverse DMA and direct/indirect HDMA when the effective B port is `$2180` and the current A address selects WRAM. Implement the side effects supported by that contract, with independent original tests.

Resolve these questions separately:

1. Does the A-bus WRAM destination receive a write?
2. Does the WMDATA pointer advance?
3. Which transferred/open-bus byte properties are actually specified?

An unspecified electrical byte must remain explicitly unverified. Any deterministic emulator approximation must be documented and tested separately from hardware-derived expectations. Do not assume either a valid copy or complete write suppression.

If the references cannot establish either write or pointer semantics, this Issue may deliver the bounded prerequisite investigation and reproducer only. Report that outcome explicitly as unresolved hardware behavior, without claiming a completed implementation.

### Specification basis

Inspect and record the relevant passages, versions and retrieval hashes from:

- [Anomie's Register Doc, revision 1157](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt): **2180 WMDATA**, **2181–2183**, **43x0 DMAPx**, **43x1 BBADx**, and **DMA AND HDMA**, especially the simultaneous WRAM-access and reverse-direction notes.
- [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm): **Work RAM Access → DMA Notes**, **Overall Memory Map / System Area**, **DMA and HDMA Channel Registers**, and **Open Bus for DMA**.

The repository records full WRAM banks `$7E/$7F`, first-8-KiB mirrors in `$00–$3F/$80–$BF`, eight-bit BBAD wrapping, constant DMA A banks, address/count progression and separate HDMA table/payload processing. It also explicitly leaves reverse electrical values unresolved. See [Issue #25 specification evidence](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f3e56850b0a9f6584a3086749e6a1647ae93a70/docs/issue-25-validation.md#specification-prerequisite) and [Issue #27 evidence and derivation limits](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f3e56850b0a9f6584a3086749e6a1647ae93a70/docs/issue-27-validation.md#specification-and-hdma-applicability). Forward quotations alone are insufficient evidence for reverse suppression.

## Context and reproduction

Planning baseline: `8f3e56850b0a9f6584a3086749e6a1647ae93a70`; supplied open-Issue inventory is empty.

Create an original one-byte reproduction with DMAP `$80`, BBAD `$80`, A address `$7E:0100`, count one, WMDATA pointer `$11000`, destination `$5A`, and WMDATA-addressed byte `$A6`. The current source predicts destination `$A6` and pointer `$11001`. This is a source-derived characterization, not a test result or hardware expectation; no tests were run during planning.

Scope includes reverse conflict classification, supported side effects, transfer progression and legal controls. Correct an earlier expectation if authoritative evidence contradicts it, documenting the correction.

Non-goals: electrical bus simulation, reverse reads of `$2181–$2183`, unrelated A-bus exclusions, DMA startup/alignment, HDMA initialization/overhead/first-frame timing, same-channel contention, enhancement chips, UI changes, and commercial ROM or firmware acquisition.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record a cited matrix separating A-bus write occurrence, WMDATA pointer effects and byte-value guarantees for general DMA and both HDMA addressing modes. Distinguish explicit specification statements, derivations and unresolved claims; emulator implementations and existing assertions are not hardware oracles.
- [ ] Add the original reproduction above. For every supported production correction, demonstrate failure against unchanged baseline production code and success after the fix. Preserve baseline observations separately from hardware assertions.
- [ ] Implement settled side effects in the shared transfer path. Classify each current A address and effective wrapping B address per byte. Preserve supported address/count/row progression and device advancement. Do not extend conflict handling to descriptor or indirect-pointer fetches solely because their table resides in WRAM.
- [ ] Cover both full WRAM banks, mirror-bank boundaries `$00/$3F/$80/$BF` at `$0000/$1FFF`, and adjacent non-WRAM `$2000` controls. Exercise fixed/incrementing/decrementing DMA, mirror entry/exit, 16-bit wrapping without bank carry, zero-count progression, all eight B patterns, mixed `$217F/$2180` accesses and BBAD wrapping. Assert only established side effects and independently derived values.
- [ ] Exercise complete direct/indirect HDMA tables with repeated and non-repeated rows and zero termination. Check table/payload pointers, line state and active masks. Separate table-bank selection from the current reverse payload destination, and avoid unspecified writes corrupting future descriptors.
- [ ] Preserve legal WMDATA-to-SRAM transfers, reverse transfers from ordinary readable B ports into WRAM, forward ROM/SRAM-to-WMDATA transfers, CPU WMDATA access and 17-bit wrap. ROM-destination controls must preserve ROM while checking supported port side effects.
- [ ] Add a bounded original CPU-executed guest for established externally observable behavior, following `tests/dma_access.rs`. Initialize through CPU instructions, record numeric results, enforce instruction/frame deadlines, and document source/data/build provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`. Do not assert an unspecified conflict byte.
- [ ] Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, and both focused DMA commands documented in [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f3e56850b0a9f6584a3086749e6a1647ae93a70/README.md#validate).
- [ ] Run the README's smoke rebuild/comparison, pinned source-built CPU/SPC suites and HDMA scanline fixture. Build cleared games twice, run `npm --prefix web ci`, `npm --prefix web run build`, and `npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'` after installing Chromium. Preserve existing game hashes, gameplay/audio assertions, deadlines, NMI/IRQ, refresh, access-boundary and HDMA-preemption regressions.
- [ ] Record actual commands/results, provenance, supported corrections and remaining uncertainty. If specification evidence remains insufficient, report a prerequisite-only result and retain unverified status; passing characterization tests cannot resolve the hardware question.

DMA and HDMA remain partial. Preserve all 24 inventory categories, scopes and existing statuses recorded in the [baseline inventory](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/8f3e56850b0a9f6584a3086749e6a1647ae93a70/docs/issue-27-validation.md#remaining-uncertainty-and-inventory). Startup/alignment, initialization, contention, electrical behavior and the broader interaction matrix remain outstanding. Limited passes establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
